mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Corsa-e electric motor replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Corsa-e electric motor replacement typically costs £2,500-£5,000 for a reconditioned drive unit supply-only, with used units from £1,500-£3,000. Fitting adds approximately 8-12 hours of labour at specialist EV rates (£80-£120/hr). Main dealer prices are typically 40-60% higher. The exact cost depends on whether you need the motor itself, the motor control unit, or the full drive assembly.

mainEntity.name: What is the "Electric Traction System Fault" on a Corsa-e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The "Electric Traction System Fault" is an increasingly common issue on the Corsa-e. The fault appears without warning and can leave the car stranded. It may be caused by software errors, motor control unit failures or wiring harness faults. A 2022 recall affected 3,666 vehicles for a software error that could result in loss of propulsion. If you see this warning, get a diagnostic immediately - caught early, a software update may resolve the issue.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the battery in a Vauxhall Corsa-e?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your Corsa-e's age, mileage and overall condition. A Vauxhall Corsa-e Electric (2020-2022) is typically worth £10,000-£18,000. A full battery pack replacement costs £5,000-£10,000. For a Corsa-e worth over £12,000, replacement is usually worthwhile, especially if the car is otherwise in good condition. For Corsa-e examples under £10,000, a battery replacement may approach or exceed the vehicle's value - evaluate carefully.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Vauxhall Corsa-e electric motor replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Corsa-e electric motor replacement typically takes 8-12 hours of labour at a specialist EV workshop. Allow 3-5 working days for the full supply-and-fit process, including delivery of the replacement unit. Main dealers may take longer due to scheduling and parts availability - specialists often offer faster turnaround.

mainEntity.name: Does the Vauxhall Corsa-e battery have a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Vauxhall Corsa-e 50kWh battery carries an 8-year / 100,000-mile warranty, guaranteeing 70% capacity retention. This warranty covers manufacturing defects and excessive degradation. Always check the warranty status of your Corsa-e before paying for a battery replacement - if the car is still within the warranty period, Vauxhall may cover the cost.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Corsa-e and Corsa Electric?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Corsa-e was the original name for Vauxhall's full-electric Corsa, launched in 2019. In 2022, the car was renamed Corsa Electric. The 2023 facelift brought revised styling and improved efficiency. The 2025 Long Range variant introduced a 51kWh battery and 156PS motor with 266-mile range. All are the same core vehicle with incremental improvements.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my Corsa-e motor with a different variant?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can, but it requires careful checking. Swapping between the 100kW (136PS) and 115kW (156PS) motors may require different battery management software, inverter calibration and potentially different wiring looms. We recommend matching the exact motor code from your existing Corsa-e to avoid compatibility issues. Use our registration lookup to confirm your motor type before ordering.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a reconditioned Corsa-e electric motor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every reconditioned Vauxhall Corsa-e electric motor and battery pack supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used drive units typically come with a shorter warranty (30-90 days) depending on the supplier - always confirm the warranty terms before purchasing. Reconditioned units also include extensive testing and diagnostics, addressing the original failure points.

historyTimeline.h2: Vauxhall Corsa-e Electric - History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Vauxhall Corsa-e was Vauxhall's first full-electric Zero Emissions vehicle, launched in 2019 as part of the fifth-generation Corsa F range. Using PSA Group technology shared with the Peugeot e-208 and DS 3 Crossback E-TENSE, the Corsa-e brought accessible EV motoring to the UK's best-selling supermini segment. Initially badged Corsa-e, it was renamed Corsa Electric in 2022.

milestones.description: Corsa-e launched with 50kWh battery, 100kW (136PS) motor, 209-mile WLTP range
Range increased to 222 miles; car renamed Corsa Electric
Mid-life facelift introduces revised styling and improved efficiency
Long Range variant debuts with 51kWh battery, 156PS motor, 266-mile range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every Corsa-e electric drive unit and battery variant is covered below, with UK replacement pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Vauxhall Corsa-e Electric - What It Costs to Fix, and When Replacement Makes Sense
commonProblems.h3: The Vauxhall Corsa-e Electric is a pioneering EV, but it's not without its issues. The 100kW motor and 50kWh battery pack have been subject to recalls and reliability concerns. Owners report traction motor faults, software glitches and battery degradation. In the 2023 What Car? Reliability Survey, the Corsa-e finished 15th out of 20 electric cars - 58% of cars that went wrong were rendered undriveable. Rebuilt drive units and battery packs through EnginesMarket include upgraded components and extensive testing, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.rootCause: The dreaded "Electric Traction System Fault" is an increasingly common issue across the Corsa-e platform. Owners report the fault appears without warning and can leave the car stranded. The issue may be linked to software errors, motor control unit failures or wiring harness faults. A 2022 recall affected 3,666 vehicles for a software error that could result in loss of propulsion.

problems.h4: Battery Degradation & Range Loss - The EV's Hidden Cost
problems.rootCause: All lithium-ion batteries degrade over time. Corsa-e owners have reported significant range loss - one owner reported using half the battery on a 60-mile daily commute, far below the claimed 200+ mile range. The 50kWh battery carries an 8-year / 100,000-mile warranty guaranteeing 70% capacity, but degradation can still be frustrating.

On a Corsa-e Electric worth £10,000-£15,000, a full battery replacement may approach or exceed 50-70% of the vehicle's value. If the car is under 8 years old and under 100,000 miles, check if the manufacturer's battery warranty covers the issue first.
problems.recommendation: Before considering battery replacement, get a full diagnostic to establish the extent of degradation. If the car is still within the 8-year / 100,000-mile warranty, claim through Vauxhall first. If degradation is severe and the car is out of warranty, compare module replacement versus full pack replacement - module replacement is often more cost-effective if only certain cells have failed.

problems.rootCause: The Corsa-e's on-board charger can fail, preventing AC charging at home or public slow chargers. The charging flap's LED system may show a solid red light indicating a malfunction. DC rapid charging may still work if the on-board charger fails, as it bypasses the on-board unit.

problems.recommendation: If your Corsa-e won't charge on AC but will charge on DC rapid chargers, the on-board charger has likely failed. Specialists can typically replace this for £1,000-£2,000 - significantly less than dealer prices. If neither AC nor DC charging works, the issue may be with the battery management system or charging port - get a full diagnostic before committing to any repair.
